notes:
The KTDB (Korea Transport Database) national passenger O/D update rebuilds the base-year (2023) trip matrix and forecasts demand to 2050. Two zone systems are reconciled: 250 si-gun-gu zones nationwide, and finer eup-myeon-dong zones inside six metro areas (Seoul Capital Area, Busan-Ulsan, Daegu, Gwangju, Daejeon-Sejong-Chungcheong, Jeju). Base-year O/D is built mode by mode: bus/rail use actual ridership statistics; private-car and other personal modes go through a five-step expansion combining travel-survey samples, telecom big data, and card/TCS data, with bidirectional and zero-cell corrections. The draft O/D is validated against observed traffic counts via cordon-line/screenline %ERROR checks and FHWA-style assignment validation, iterating until errors meet tolerance. Socioeconomic indicators (population, employment, enrollment, land-use plans) are projected per target year, then a standard four-step model (generation/attraction, distribution, mode split, assignment) is applied consistently across national and regional models to produce future O/D matrices.

Reviewer triage (2026-09-15, applies wave-wide to the 2026-09 KMP submissions): the submitted answers mirrored the seoul listing's data profile but are contradicted by the stated methodology and the shipped bundles. Workplace totals are KTDB all-purpose attraction trip-ends (jobs run 2–3× residents on every map in the wave; commuterPopulation = population/1.2 exactly on all six), not a census of workplace employment — scored estimated_proxy; this listing sits inside one of the six KTDB regional models, so zone counts and the O/D matrix carry eup-myeon-dong grain (adm4). Within-zone placement carries no workplace-specific signal: job/resident ratios are flat across functionally opposite districts (Changwon National Industrial Complex 2.08 vs citywide 1.95 vs a residential new town 2.18; in suwon, Samsung Digital City 2.71 vs the Yeongtong residential district 2.44), so workplace intensity is size_only on the ~400 m demand-node lattice (mesh_500). The resident side keeps the SGIS grid claim: total_population at mesh_250 source grain (scaled by the fixed 1/1.2 constant), aggregated to the same lattice (mesh_500, measured_per_unit). The O/D is the KTDB expansion-built all-purpose matrix (travel-survey samples + telecom + card/TCS data, assignment-validated) — priced structured_marginals under the sampled/constructed-blend rule at the zone grain. Parity anchor: the seoul listing's observed telecom commuting matrix scores structured_marginals @ adm4; an expansion-built all-purpose matrix cannot outrank it.
